papers.title: Closed layers in tensor-triangular geometry
papers.abstract: In the absence of a theory of closed immersions in tensor-triangular geometry, we propose an alternative approach via quotients of module categories. As an application, we prove invariance of homological residue fields under completion.

papers.title: Hermitian K-theory for stable $\infty$-categories IV: Karoubi-Grothendieck-Witt theory
papers.abstract:
In analogy with the passage from connective to non-connective algebraic K-theory, Schlichting put forward the Karoubi-Grothendieck-Witt spectrum as an approximation to Grothendieck-Witt theory by a functor invariant under idempotent completion. In this paper, we extend his construction to the setting of Poincar\'e $\infty$-categories and characterise the resulting functor by the expected universal property.
  Our main result places these Karoubi-Grothendieck-Witt-spectra in an exact sequence involving the ultimately decorated L-spectrum and homotopy orbits of non-connective K-theory. This confirms a conjecture of Williams which had remained open even for rings in which $2$ is invertible, and allows us to deduce universal characterisations for ultimately decorated L-theory. We obtain these results by unifying the Bass-Heller-Swan and Ranicki-Shaneson splittings into a general decomposition theorem that yields, in particular, formulas for Grothendieck-Witt groups of Laurent polynomial rings.
  Finally, we construct multiplicative structures on both versions of our Grothendieck-Witt and L-functors and refine their universal properties to multiplicative ones. Along the way, we show that the original versions are even idempotent with respect to Day convolution.

papers.title: Non-abelian $p$-adic Hodge theory and stacks
papers.abstract: In the first half of these notes, we survey some aspects of the stack-theoretic perspective on $p$-adic Hodge theory, with an emphasis on the non-abelian aspects. In the second half, we report ongoing joint work on ``quantizing'' non-abelian $p$-adic Hodge theory.

papers.title: An Equivariant Coarse Green-Julg Theorem for Proper Actions
papers.abstract: We prove an equivariant coarse Green--Julg theorem for proper isometric actions of countable discrete groups on bounded geometry metric spaces. We introduce the $(\Gamma, X)$-controlled proper $C^{*}$-algebra, and show that the evaluation-at-zero map between the equivariant localization and Roe algebras with such coefficients induces an isomorphism on $K$-theory.

papers.title: Higher Galois Recognition and Parameter Descent
papers.abstract: Let $n\geq0$ and let $\mathcal X$ be a bounded coherent $\infty$-topos. Suppose that finitely many noninitial coherent $n$-truncated objects cover its terminal object, and that every coherent $n$-truncated object in each of their slices has a finite covering family of sections. We identify $\mathcal X^{\mathrm{coh}}_{\leq n}$ with $\operatorname{Fun}(M,\mathcal S_{\pi,\leq n})$ for a $\pi$-finite $(n+1)$-type $M$, recovered by all finite models preserving finite limits, finite coproducts, and effective epimorphisms. Descent uses degrees through $n+2$ for objects and $n+1$ for maps; both bounds are sharp for finite homotopy actions. Every exact functor $F$ between recognized categories has a universal parameter $P_F=F_!(1)$ and a canonical factorization through its slice with fully faithful second functor. This parameter characterizes full faithfulness, conservativity, and all exact slice factorizations. For successive abelian Postnikov layers, we identify the space of marked exact lifts with a path space of Eilenberg--Mac Lane sections with local coefficients. The obstruction, classes of lifts, and relative automorphisms occur in degrees $r+1$, $r$, and $r-1$. We compute a twisted parity obstruction and, for odd primes, classify cyclic self-equivalence components by a $p$-adic valuation. A nonzero Postnikov class can persist in the identity component. For continuous finite families over a profinite $(n+1)$-type, we prove that a uniform finite-section atlas exists precisely when the complete model space is $\pi$-finite. Exact functors from finite model semantics, together with their lift spaces, satisfy finite-stage descent, while explicit profinite examples separate objectwise trivialization from uniform parameter elimination.

papers.title: Vanishing Theorem of Pin(2)-equivariant Bauer-Furuta Invariants as Stable Sections
papers.abstract: We develop a viewpoint of Pin(2)-equivariant Bauer-Furuta invariant: It can be converted to a section over a finite dimensional Pin(2)-orbit, and it takes values in ordinary stable homotopy class. This viewpoint reveals a topological limitation of the invariant: If the fiber's connectivity exceeds the dimension of the base space, then all sections are homotopic to the trivial section. We use it to recover Lin-Mukherjee vanishing theorem. Furthermore, the family Seiberg-Witten invariant can be obtained from the pullback of such sections to $S^1$-orbit. We use this fact to prove a vanishing theorem of the Pin(2)-equivariant family Bauer-Furuta invariant after two stabilizations.

papers.title: Pre-Model Structures on the Category of $C_p$-Sets
papers.abstract: It is a folk theorem of Goodwillie that there are exactly 9 model structures on the category of sets, coming from 18 pre-model structures. We investigate model structures and pre-model structures on the category of $G$-sets for a finite group $G$. We outline a strategy for finding all model structures in this category, and partially execute this strategy for the case of $C_p$-sets, where $C_p$ denotes a cyclic group of prime order $p$. In particular, there are exactly 1777 pre-model structures on the category of $C_p$-sets.

papers.title: The Ultimate Matching Theorem
papers.abstract: Let $X_1,\dots,X_N$ be independent uniform points in the unit square, matched either to an evenly spread deterministic configuration or to a second independent sample. For exponents $\alpha_1,\alpha_2>2$ with $1/\alpha_1+1/\alpha_2=1/2$, we prove that with probability tending to one a single permutation controls the $j$th coordinate displacements in the exponential Orlicz norm of exponent $\alpha_j$, at the scale $\sqrt{\log N/N}$, for both $j=1,2$. This settles Talagrand's Ultimate Matching Conjecture for all pairs of finite critical exponents. The proof constructs, on the flat torus, a current whose divergence is Gaussian white noise projected on a dyadic grid and whose coordinates have the critical anisotropic exponential Orlicz bounds, and transfers it to matching through a primal optimal-transport reduction. At the hard endpoints $(2,\infty)$ and $(\infty,2)$ the conjecture fails: a Brownian local-time construction shows that the normalized optimal matching cost diverges in probability.

papers.title: Gaussian limits for non-cyclic and elementary abelian Sylow subgroups of the multiplicative group
papers.abstract: We study the number of non-cyclic Sylow subgroups of $(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)^\times$. Pollack suggested investigating whether this count has a limiting distribution after suitable normalization. For uniformly chosen $n\le x$, we prove a Gaussian limit with variance asymptotic to $\tfrac12\log_2x/\log_3x$. Motivated by the fixed-rank normal-order results of Morales, Polanco, and Pollack, we further prove joint Gaussian limits for this count and the numbers of elementary abelian Sylow subgroups of any fixed finite collection of ranks at least two. We give explicit prime-sum centers and asymptotics for all arithmetic covariances. The same joint theorem includes the number of common prime divisors of Euler's and Dedekind's functions. The proof uses the integer Kubilius model, estimates for the dependence between distinct output primes, and mean-square bounds for arithmetic truncation.

papers.title: Geometric Hammocks: Surface Laminations and the Ziegler Spectrum of String Algebras
papers.abstract: We give the first complete topological, geometric, and ergodic classification of the Ziegler spectrum $\Zg(\Lambda)$ of a non-domestic string algebra $\Lambda$ over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary cardinality, via a dictionary with Thurston's theory of geodesic laminations on a cusped hyperbolic surface. This is a model-theoretic counterpart of Haiden--Katzarkov--Kontsevich's realization (\emph{Publ.\ Math.\ IHES} 2017) of stability conditions on the bounded derived category of a gentle algebra via flat surfaces: pure-injective modules correspond to admissible geodesics, and the Ziegler topology to a corridor quotient of Chabauty space. Three consequences follow. The Krull--Gabriel dimension equals the surface's topological accumulation depth, and the string closure with all higher Cantor--Bendixson strata is globally homeomorphic to an explicit corridor space, with the pushout map to $\Zg(\Lambda)$ a homeomorphism if and only if $\Lambda$ is domestic. Prefix-free dyadic blocks in the geometric perfect core verify Puninski's cardinality-free two-chain criterion, resolving the open problem of superdecomposable pure-injectives over uncountable fields for all non-domestic string and special biserial algebras. Three purely algebraic invariants on the perfect core---localized pp-shape entropy, a $K_0$-weighted pressure function satisfying an algebraic Ruelle--Walters Variational Principle, and a pp-bifurcation index with a Gauss--Bonnet simplicity obstruction---strictly separate uncountable iso-entropic and iso-pressure families, and the inverse limit of the quotient pp-lattice recovers the transversal Cantor cross-section.

papers.title: Linear circle quotients of products of odd-dimensional spheres: classification and geometric applications
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the orbit manifolds of free diagonal linear circle actions on \(S^{2n+1}\times S^{2n+1}\). For every \(n\geq 1\), we establish a PL homeomorphism classification of the orbit manifolds in terms of the weights of the actions. We also obtain diffeomorphism classification and homotopy classification of such orbit manifolds in dimension $9$ and $13$. The diffeomorphism classification results lead to two geometric applications. For every \(m\geq 1\), there exist a non-spin \(9\)-manifold \(M_m^9\) and a spin \(13\)-manifold \(M_m^{13}\) in our family such that the moduli space of unit-volume homogeneous Einstein metrics on each manifold has at least \(2^{m-1}\) connected components. Moreover, each of these manifolds admits at least \(2^{m-1}\) regular Sasakian structures whose underlying contact structures are pairwise non-contactomorphic.

papers.title: Thom Morphisms, Self-Intersection, and the Sectional Category of a Section
papers.abstract: For sections between simply connected spaces of finite rational type, we compare module sectional category, sectional category and relative category after rationalization. Fibre Poincar\'e duality turns the compatibility of derived evaluation with the section into a derived self-intersection formula. We prove equality of the three invariants under any of four hypotheses: a base-dimension bound, finite total rational homotopy of the fibre, a smooth section with closed manifold fibre, or a compatible relative Frobenius model. Projective bundles over CP^k with fibre CP^r have common value k + r, which is unbounded even for fixed fibre. Whether fibre Poincar\'e duality alone suffices remains open.

papers.title: $2$-adic integral models of some Shimura varieties with parahoric level structure
papers.abstract: We construct integral models over $p=2$ for some Shimura varieties of abelian type with parahoric level structure, extending the previous work of Kim-Madapusi, Kisin, Pappas, and Zhou. These integral models are canonical in the sense of Pappas-Rapoport.

papers.title: $5I(K_X+\Delta)$ is very ample on stable log surfaces
papers.abstract:
We prove that Bombieri's bound for canonical models of surfaces of general type extends to stable log surfaces, that is, $mI(K_X+\Delta)$ is very ample for every $m\geq 5$ and every stable log surface $(X,\Delta)$ over $\mathbb{C}$ with reduced boundary and global Cartier index $I$.
  On the way to this result we determine the cases where $|3I(K_X+\Delta)|$ has base points.

papers.title: A Complete Classification of Maximal Hyperelliptic Curves Related to Chebyshev Polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $\varphi_d$ be the Chebyshev polynomial with $\varphi_d(t+t^{-1})=t^d+t^{-d}$, and let $H_d$ be the hyperelliptic curve $y^2=\varphi_d(x)$. We determine all pairs $(d,p)$, with $p\nmid2d$ prime, for which $H_d$ is maximal over some finite field of characteristic $p$, together with all such fields. For $p\equiv1\pmod4$ only partial results were known. In this case, for odd $d$ we show that the Jacobian of $H_d$ is supersingular if and only if $H_d$ is maximal over a finite extension of $\mathbb{F}_p$, and that this happens precisely when $d=\ell^n$ with $\ell\equiv1\pmod4$ prime and $p$ a generator of $(\mathbb{Z}/\ell^n\mathbb{Z})^\times$; we also compute the Frobenius polynomial. Necessity comes from the Shimura--Taniyama formula together with the non-vanishing of the value at $0$ of certain Dirichlet L-series and information about the action of Frobenius on $2$-torsion. The case of even $d$ and $p\equiv1\pmod 4$ follows from the odd case, by a short reduction.

papers.title: A conditional proof of the Casas-Alvero conjecture
papers.abstract: The Casas-Alvero conjecture states that if $f(X)$ is a monic univariate polynomial of degree $d$ over a characteristic $0$ field $\mathbb{K}$ such that $\gcd(f, f_{i})$ is non-trivial for each $i=1, \dots, d-1$, then $f(X)=(X-\alpha)^d$ for some $\alpha\in \mathbb{K}$. In this paper, we prove the Casas-Alvero conjecture for polynomials of any degree $d\geq 3$ over any characteristic $0$ field, under a uniform local {\L}ojasiewicz type hypothesis for a family of polynomials obtained from the elementary symmetric functions. Furthermore, we prove this estimate on compact subsets of a common Zariski open set of coefficients parametrizing the family.

papers.title: A Counterexample to the Subtraction-Free Conjecture for Bounded Ratios of Minors
papers.abstract: We disprove the subtraction-free conjecture of Boocher and Froehle for bounded ratios of minors of totally positive matrices. We construct products (P,M,Q) of ordinary minors of a matrix of order (3207) such that [ 0<\frac{P}{MQ}\leq\frac1{64} ] throughout the totally positive locus, whereas (MQ-P) has a coefficient equal to (-1) in the standard bidiagonal parameters.

papers.title: A cyclotomic Artin-Tate formula and sphere packing for K3 surfaces
papers.abstract: We give new necessary conditions on the Weil polynomial of a K3 surface over a finite field using techniques from the theory of sphere packing. By comparing the Artin-Tate formula over a finite extension, we derive a special values formula at roots of unity that involves the discriminant of the Frobenius coinvariant lattice. Known bounds on the minimum discriminants of even rootless lattices then imply nontrivial lower bounds on these special values. Applying these new conditions to Kedlaya and Sutherland's list of candidate Weil polynomials of K3 surfaces over the field with 2 elements rules out over 50% of the candidates.

papers.title: A decomposition theorem for minimal W-algebras of type A
papers.abstract:
To any simple Lie algebra, one can associate a minimal affine W-algebra. It is a vertex algebra which is obtained from the universal affine vertex algebra by a chiral Hamiltonian reduction procedure. This reduction is determined by data coming from the minimal nilpotent orbit. It is a chiral quantisation of the Slodowy slice associated to this minimal orbit.
  In this paper, when the simple Lie algebra is of type A, we prove that the minimal W-algebra is isomorphic to a commutant subalgebra in a localisation of the universal affine vertex algebra. Then, we establish a decomposition theorem \`a la Losev: the localised universal affine vertex algebra decomposes as the tensor product of the minimal affine W-algebra and another vertex subalgebra. As a direct corollary, we retrieve the celebrated result of inverse Hamiltonian reduction for the minimal W-algebra.
  We also prove an analogue of this result for the corresponding finite W-algebra. In both cases, our approach relies on the geometry of the associated Slodowy slice.

papers.title: A linear gap for the maximal cp-rank
papers.abstract: We prove that the maximal cp-rank $p_n$ satisfies $p_n\ge n(n-3)/2$ for odd $n\ge5$ and $p_n\ge n(n-3)/2-1$ for even $n\ge6$. Together with the known upper bound $p_n\le\binom{n+1}{2}-4$, this gives $p_n=n^2/2+O(n)$.

papers.title: A Michael Space in the Laver model
papers.abstract: We show that a Michael space exists in the Laver model.

papers.title: A Proof of the Second brick-Brauer-Thrall Conjecture for $E$-infinite algebras
papers.abstract: For any finite-dimensional algebra $A$ over an algebraically closed field, we prove that if $A$ is $E$-infinite, then the Second brick-Brauer-Thrall Conjecture holds for $A$. In fact, we show that if there is a rational ray outside the $\tau$-tilting fan of $A$, then $A$ admits an infinite family of $\theta$-stable bricks of dimension $d$, for some positive integer $d$ and weight $\theta$. To show our main result, from any $\tau$-regular component of $A$ with no dense orbit, we obtain a brick component that also has no dense orbit and whose points in general position are $\theta$-stable modules for a given weight $\theta$. As an important consequence, we conclude that $A$ is stably-discrete (also called multiplicity-free) if and only if $A$ is $E$-finite. Moreover, we prove that Demonet's (lattice point) Conjecture implies the stable Second brick-Brauer-Thrall Conjecture. For $E$-infinite algebras, our results settle several open conjectures. Together with our earlier work and recent developments, this leads to important reductions in the study of some challenging open problems.

papers.title: A torsion theoretic interpretation for sheaves of modules and Grothendieck topologies on directed categories
papers.abstract: We prove that every Grothendieck topology induces a hereditary torsion pair in the category of presheaves of modules on a ringed site, and obtain a homological characterization of sheaves of modules: a presheaf of modules is a sheaf of modules if and only if it is saturated with respect to torsion presheaves, or equivalently, it is right perpendicular to torsion presheaves in the sense of Geigle and Lenzing. We also study Grothendieck topologies on directed categories $\mathscr{C}$ satisfying certain finiteness condition, and show that every Grothendieck topology on $\mathscr{C}$ is a subcategory topology if and only if $\mathscr{C}$ is an artinian EI category. Consequently, in this case every sheaf category is equivalent to the presheaf category over a full subcategory of $\mathscr{C}$. Finally, we classify all Grothendieck topologies on a special type of noetherian EI categories, and extend the locally self-injective property of representations of $\mathrm{F}$ and $\mathrm{VI}$ to representations of their infinite full subcategories. Some potential applications in group representation theory are given at the end of this paper.

papers.title: Addendum and Corrigendum to: Some homological properties of category $\mathcal{O}$, V
papers.abstract: In various special cases, we provide an alternative argument for equivalence between Kostant positivity of some involutions in type $A$ and the conjunction of the categorical K{\aa}hrstr{\"o}m's condition for these involutions with indecomposability of the images of the corresponding simple modules in category $\mathcal{O}$ under projective functors.

papers.title: Affine Springer fibers, Cherednik algebra modules and Hilbert schemes: torus link case
papers.abstract: For a pair of positive integers $M,N$ with GCD $d$, we relate the bigraded $S_N\times S_d$-Frobenius characters of the homology of the positive part of a homogeneous affine Springer fiber for $\mathrm{GL}_N$ of slope $M/N$ to a direct sum of the associated graded of minimal supported modules of type $A_{N-1}$ rational Cherednik algebra at the same slope, and to the equivariant K-theory of a coherent sheaf on the Hilbert scheme of points on the plane. For the first object, we use the Hessenberg paving of Goresky-Kottwitz-Macpherson; for the second and third objects, we resort to an explicit Hodge module on $\mathfrak{sl}_N$. The bridge between them is a non-coprime shuffle theorem of Kim-Oh.

papers.title: Algebraic K-theory of geometric fields: rigidity
papers.abstract:
In this paper we consider the problem of Galois descent for suitably completed algebraic K-theory of fields. One of the main results in the present paper is a suitable form of rigidity for Borel-style generalized equivariant cohomology with respect to certain spectra, which includes mod-${\ell}$ Algebraic K-theory, for $\ell$ -invertible in the base field. Such a rigidity theorem in fact provides a determination of the mod-$\ell$ Algebraic K-theory of geometric fields, i.e., fields that contain an algebraically closed sub-field in terms of the absolute Galois group of the bigger field and proves one conjecture due to the first author.
  What remains in a proof of a related conjecture of the first author (see [C13]) is a derived completion theorem for equivariant algebraic K-theory with respect to the action of profinite groups. Such a derived completion theorem, with certain restrictions, is proven in the paper, [CJ26-2]. What we do in the remaining part of this paper is to provide a comparison of the generalized Borel style equivariant K-theory considered in [CJ26-2] and also in [C13], with the generalized Borel style equivariant K-theory defined using more standard models of geometric classifying spaces. This enables us to apply the rigidity results proven in this paper to the generalized Borel style equivariant K-theory considered in [CJ26-2], thereby enabling us to provide an affirmative solution to the above mentioned conjecture in many cases.

papers.title: An exact moment criterion for survival under renewed spatial catastrophes
papers.abstract: We prove an exact moment criterion for survival in a binary growth process subject to independently renewed spatial catastrophes. Occupied sites spread through a finite set of allowed increments on the integer lattice, and Poisson catastrophes with unbounded cube sizes empty all occupied sites in each affected cube. Under finite one-site hitting intensity, a positive finite-seed survival phase exists if and only if the cube-size measure has a finite moment of order one more than the spatial dimension. The divergent endpoint yields extinction at every positive intensity. The proof centres on a one-dimensional positive-phase construction for connected interval errors under a finite second moment. Extremal-path resampling gives a conditional correlation inequality, which controls exact interval insertion counts and a finite-history potential. Coordinate restriction and envelope covering then establish the criterion in every dimension. We also prove the bulk-to-seed reversal identity and extend the criterion to uniformly fat shapes. For the one-sided one-dimensional rule, the stationary hole density has a quadratic dilute expansion under the same second-moment condition. Its excess over independently eroded Poisson events is strictly positive at every positive intensity, with an explicit quadratic coefficient in the dilute limit.

papers.title: Another proof of quantum Laurent positivity, II
papers.abstract: We give a further combinatorial proof of Laurent positivity for skew-symmetric quantum cluster algebras.

papers.title: Arcs on rational double points in arbitrary characteristic
papers.abstract: We settle the Nash problem for two-dimensional rational double points in all characteristics. The proof is based on a direct computation of the families of arcs through these singularities.

papers.title: Asymptotically good codes from Siegel modular varieties
papers.abstract: We construct asymptotically good codes by evaluating Siegel modular forms at superspecial points on congruence towers of Siegel modular varieties. For every genus $g\ge2$ and every fixed weight $w\ge g+1$, the construction gives such a family in sufficiently large characteristic, over a finite field which is independent of the level of the tower. The towers can be chosen so that this field is $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$. We give an explicit lower bound for the asymptotic rate. The lower bound for the relative minimum distance follows from the Pieri formula on the space of flags in the Hodge bundle and an intersection argument along its strata. We also prove that, for $p\ge5$ and $0\le w\le p+1$, the kernel of evaluation in every genus consists precisely of the multiples of the ordinary Hasse invariant. For $g=2,3$, the geometry of the supersingular locus gives explicit bounds for the relative minimum distance and recovery sets whose sizes are bounded independently of the level.

papers.title: Broué's Abelian Defect Group Conjecture for 2-Blocks
papers.abstract: We prove that every 2-block of a finite group with an abelian defect group is splendidly Rickard equivalent to its Brauer correspondent.

papers.title: Canonical Volumes of Threefolds with Positive Geometric Genus
papers.abstract: We prove that a complex projective threefold of general type with canonical singularities and positive geometric genus has canonical volume at least $1/30$, with strict inequality when its Euler characteristic is positive. We describe the equality cases as canonical hypersurfaces of degree $28$ in $\mathbb P(1,3,4,5,14)$. These canonical models and their smooth projective resolutions are simply connected. Their coarse moduli space is irreducible and rational of dimension $103$, with finite quotient singularities; all admissible $\mathbb Q$-Gorenstein deformations are unobstructed and arise by varying the equation.

papers.title: Cayley graphs of abelian groups and their quantum symmetries
papers.abstract: Building on the recent work of Marashdeh on the circulant graphs of prime order, we study the quantum symmetries of the Cayley graphs of the finite abelian groups $A$. Our main result states that if the coherent algebra is the orbital algebra of $A\rtimes E$, with $|E|=k$ and with the non-trivial elements of $E$ having at most $m$ fixed points, then the graph has no quantum symmetry when $|A|\geq k^2m$. We also settle the case of the circulant graphs with $p^n$ vertices.

papers.title: Classifiyng metrically conical rational singularities
papers.abstract:
We will in this article classify which rational complex surface singularities are metrically conical, that is have the bilipschitz type of their inner metric equivalent to that of a cone. This is done using the thick-thin decomposition for the inner geometry of a normal complex surface singularity and properties of rational singularities.
  The result is a family of singularities depending only on their topology which is given as a $3$-parameter family.

papers.title: Closing the identification step in the GFF limit: Uniqueness of the zero-slope six-vertex phase for −1 ≤ Δ < 1/2
papers.abstract: For the six-vertex model with $a=b=1$ and $c\in(1,2]$, that is $-1\le\Delta<\frac{1}{2}$, we prove that the plane measure, the limit of balanced torus measures, is the only translation-ergodic gradient Gibbs measure of slope zero, and hence the unique translation-invariant minimiser of the specific free energy. Both statements had been asserted by reference to Sheffield's uniqueness theory, which is proved for nearest-neighbour potentials; we show that for $c\ne1$ the six-vertex weights, which couple faces across the diagonals of each vertex, are not a nearest-neighbour potential in height coordinates. The proof extends Sheffield's cluster swapping to these diagonal interactions by means of residual energies on the diagonals, shows with the Lanford–Ruelle theorem for subshifts of finite type and a Burton–Keane argument that two distinct ergodic zero-slope phases are gradients of Gibbs measures on heights, and shows from the spin representation in the form given by Duminil-Copin, Kozlowski, Lammers and Manolescu that the plane measure is not. This supplies a step that we found missing in the chain of recent results on the Gaussian free field limit of the six-vertex height function. An unrefereed manuscript of OpenAI states the full-plane limit for every $c\in(0,2]$; for $\sqrt{2}\le c<2$ it identifies a state built from nearly balanced sectors with the plane measure through the characterisation above. Our result gives that identification, given two properties of the state stated in the manuscript. We also check that the manuscript and the work of Averous, Duminil-Copin, He, Lammers and Manolescu concern the same measure, so that their convergence in domains holds, for $c\in[1,2]$ and with constants depending on $\Delta$, wherever the manuscript's full-plane theorem holds.

papers.title: Cluster-theoretic Newton--Okounkov polytopes of flag varieties of types $A_4$ and $B_2$
papers.abstract: Newton--Okounkov bodies have been used for studying toric degenerations of flag varieties. We classify the Newton--Okounkov polytopes associated with cluster valuations and the anticanonical line bundle on full flag varieties of types $A_4$ and $B_2$. In type $A_4$, the $672$ seeds of cluster type $D_6$ yield $162$ affine unimodular equivalence classes, which coincide with the combinatorial equivalence classes. We determine the subgroup of exchange-graph automorphisms preserving every polytope class. It is a Klein four group of index six in the automorphism group of the exchange graph of cluster type $D_6$. In type $B_2$, we give defining inequalities for all six seeds. At the anticanonical weight, the two combinatorial equivalence classes split into three affine unimodular equivalence classes. Their respective class-preserving automorphism groups have orders four and two.

papers.title: Computing weighted sheaf cohomology using noncommutative differential modules
papers.abstract: We describe a novel method for computing sheaf cohomology over weighted projective spaces and stacks using exterior algebra and differential module techniques, generalizing an algorithm due to Eisenbud-Fl{\o}ystad-Schreyer over projective space.

papers.title: Contravariant Koszul duality between non-positive and positive dg algebras
papers.abstract: We study contravariant Koszul duality between locally finite non-positive and positive dg algebras. We characterize a finiteness condition on the positive side, called pvd-finiteness, in terms of Hom-finiteness of the perfectly valued derived category, local finiteness of the Koszul dual, and the existence of an injective cogenerator in the canonical heart. Under this condition, Koszul duality exchanges perfect and perfectly valued derived categories, and it gives a bijection between quasi-isomorphism classes of locally finite non-positive and pvd-finite positive dg algebras. We also show that the derived category of a pvd-finite positive dg algebra is co-approximable in the sense of Rahul, and that the perfect and perfectly valued derived categories of such an algebra determine each other through finite cohomological functors. As applications, we give a Morita-type characterization of these triangulated categories and show that a bounded heart of such a category is a length category if and only if it is functorially finite.

papers.title: COUNTABLY INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SPACES OF CRYSTALLINE MEASURES
papers.abstract: We construct a symmetric locally finite set Λ ⊂ R for which the space MΛ of crystalline measures with support and spectrum in Λ has countably infinite Hamel dimension; Meyer asked what the dimension of such spaces can be. More precisely, there is a sequence of crystalline measures such that every element of MΛ is a unique finite linear combination of them. Every layer of MΛ of fixed Hermite–Sobolev order is finite-dimensional, but the layer dimensions are unbounded; in one construction they grow linearly, and in general their growth can be prescribed up to a linear change of the order. (For every locally finite set the dimension is finite, countably infinite or equal to the continuum, and the countable case is exactly this behaviour of the layers.) The construction uses clusters of atoms that imitate derivatives of Dirac masses, which produce one-dimensional blocks of prescribed Hermite order. The main difficulty is to show that the union of infinitely many blocks supports no other crystalline measures. We prove this by placing the blocks at random scales, separated by rapidly growing gaps, and showing that every element of fixed Hermite order splits into finitely many block components. We also obtain disjoint sets A, B such that the crystalline measures with support in B and spectrum in A form a countably infinite-dimensional space, while MA = MB = {0}. The existence statement, without the symmetry of Λ, has been formalised and machine-checked in Lean 4; the formal development is recorded in Palomar

papers.title: Cutoff for q-deformed classical card shuffles in the type A Iwahori--Hecke algebra
papers.abstract: We study the mixing behavior of three q-deformed card shuffles on $\mathcal{H}_q(S_n)$: the short systematic scan introduced in \cite{DiaconisRam2000}, the $q$--deformed random--to--random shuffle introduced in \cite{AxelrodFreedBraunerChiangComminsLang2024}, and the $q$--deformed $k$--star transposition shuffle, whose $q=1$ counterpart was studied in \cite{ArfaeeNestoridi}. The first two chains were diagonalized in \cite{DiaconisRam2000} and \cite{AxelrodFreedBraunerChiangComminsLang2024}, respectively. Here, we diagonalize the $q$--deformed $k$--star transposition shuffle and use the spectra of the three chains to study their mixing behavior. For fixed $q>1$, we prove that all three exhibit total variation and $\ell^2$ cutoff. For the short systematic scan, these improve both the upper and lower bounds of Diaconis and Ram \cite{DiaconisRam2000}.

papers.title: Definability and Lifting in Model Subgroupoids
papers.abstract: Restriction to a wide subgroupoid of a model groupoid can introduce invariant relations, maps, and objects. For open topological groupoids, a map between restricted objects lifts exactly when its graph is invariant under the full groupoid, and a specified quotient presentation lifts exactly when its kernel relation is invariant. Under coherent restriction, these criteria recover definable maps and coherent quotient presentations. For finite continuous actions of a group with an open subgroup of finite index, coinduction identifies extensions with invariant subsets on which evaluation is bijective. For a finite group $G$ and a normal subgroup $N$, we classify extensions of finite $N$-sets by normalizer extensions of their orbit types. Multiplicities must be constant on conjugacy orbits of types; within each such block, the liftable multiplicities form the additive monoid generated by indices of subgroups over which the normalizer extension splits. The same subgroup data determine the groupoid of lifts and its isomorphism-class and mass generating functions. This classification also applies to finite continuous actions of profinite groups with an open normal subgroup. For a fixed action, a centralizer extension gives the splitting obstruction, with an $H^2$ obstruction and an $H^1$ classification when its kernel is abelian. The center of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb F_5)$ gives the monoid $\langle12,20\rangle$; Heisenberg groups over fields of odd prime order give unbounded lifting indices at fixed cohomological period. Finite torsor theories and infinite pure sets realize the definability criteria. For profinite extensions with finite kernel, one finite quotient detects all liftable multiplicities, though it need not carry every lift.

papers.title: Differential Monodromy, $q$-Opers, and Universal $(G,q)$-Wronskians
papers.abstract: We give a geometric formulation of the $q$DE/ODE/IM correspondence for families of differential operators associated with simple Lie algebras of ADE type. Under analytic hypotheses, the $q$-connection associated with shifted monodromy defines a twisted $(G,q)$-oper and has Steinberg form in the frame of solutions normalized by prescribed asymptotics in a sector at infinity. We identify the central connection between the normalized solution frames at zero and infinity with a universal meromorphic $(G,q)$-Wronskian. Its generalized minors give $Q$-functions satisfying the ADE $QQ$-relations. When $q$ is not a root of unity, we parametrize shifted monodromy by quantum-affine $q$-characters evaluated on shifted $Q$-ratios, using the same character formulas that describe normalized transfer-matrix eigenvalues. We verify the analytic hypotheses for generic untwisted Feigin--Frenkel--Hernandez affine opers, thereby relating these affine opers to twisted $(G,q)$-opers.

papers.title: E-symmetric algebras II
papers.abstract: We introduce generalized Jacobian algebras and show that a finite-dimensional algebra is E-symmetric if and only if it is generalized Jacobian. We also characterize E-symmetric algebras in terms of its simple modules. We show that Enomoto's counterexample to the Periodicity Conjecture is a generalized Jacobian algebra, which is not Jacobian in the classical sense.

papers.title: Energy complexity and dissipation of noisy consensus
papers.abstract: We characterize the signal-energy complexity of distributed agreement over independent Gaussian point-to-point channels. For $n$ processes deciding $L$ binary coordinates under coordinatewise unanimity validity and a joint failure probability of at most $\varepsilon$, every finite causal protocol requires a worst-input expected signal energy of $\Omega(N_0n[L+\ln(n/\varepsilon)])$. This lower bound combines two distinct mechanisms: an exact relative-entropy identity for locally interchanged reception histories yields the reliability term even in the presence of shared randomness and active noisy feedback, while a coordinatewise direct-sum argument establishes the payload term. In the fault-free setting, a deterministic fixed-leader protocol attains this optimal order for all $0<\varepsilon\leq1/8$. In the presence of $f\leq(1/3-\kappa)n$ static Byzantine faults, the same order is achieved in the polynomial-error regime $\varepsilon\geq n^{-a}$ via public committee sampling and robust joint decoding within explicit finite storage and computation budgets. Consequently, batching amortizes the reliability overhead, yielding an energy cost of $\Theta(N_0n[1+L^{-1}\ln(n/\varepsilon)])$ per coordinate. We then connect this communication optimum to physical dissipation through a stochastic-thermodynamic model of a thermal channel port. Under a non-recovering mode replacement interface, the communication converse translates directly into lower bounds on entropy production and, when the endpoint mean internal energies agree, cyclic work. When work recovery is permitted prior to mode reset, we derive the exact minimum reset entropy production within a bounded-displacement control class as a function of the information accessible to the recovery controller, thereby separating the fundamental communication cost from its control-dependent thermodynamic realization.

papers.title: Essential $p$-dimension of simple algebras and noncrossed products of prime exponent
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and $F$ a field of characteristic different from $p$. For integers $n\ge2$ and $1\le m\le n$, we complete the determination of the essential $p$-dimension of the class of central simple algebras of degree $p^n$ and exponent dividing $p^m$. In particular, we have $\operatorname{ed}_p(\operatorname{PGL}(p^n))=p^{2n-2}+1$, extending a result of Merkurjev for $n=2$. Using the comparison theorem of Chernousov and Merkurjev, we also determine the essential $p$-dimension of every split simple group of type $A$. To obtain the lower bounds, we apply a theorem of Ofek to block centralizers. As an application, we prove the existence of division algebras of exponent $p$ over field extensions of $F$ which remain noncrossed products after any field extension of degree prime to $p$, and answer in the negative a problem in the survey by Auel, Brussel, Garibaldi, and Vishne. The algebras can be chosen to have degree $p^n$ for every $n\ge3$ if $p$ is odd and every $n\ge4$ if $p=2$. For $p=2$ and every $n\ge3$, we also determine the essential $2$-dimensions of the classes of central simple algebras of degree $2^n$ with orthogonal involution and with symplectic involution.

papers.title: Finite Numerical Joyce Transport and Derived Hall Scattering Groupoid
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a triangulated category over a finite field $k$ satisftying certain finiteness conditions. Let $\Sigma$ be a connected component of the space of numerical stability conditions on $\mathcal{D}$ with one element $\sigma\in\Sigma$ satisfying the support property and the finite counting condition. We prove that each of the Joyce elements with respect to $\sigma_1\in\Sigma$ is a finite rational Lie polynomial in those of any other $\sigma_0\in\Sigma$, so the generated Lie subalgebra $\mathfrak{L}_\sigma,\sigma\in\Sigma$ in the uncompleted derived Hall algebra $\mathcal{H}(\mathcal{D})$ is constant on $\Sigma$. Our proof combines completions on strict sectors with a uniform mass bound for successive local substitutions. We use the method of Hall scattering diagrams on phase categories to provide a realization of the transform of Joyce elements. For the finite-length case, we also give an alternative proof using finite-length hearts instead of phase categories. As an application, we explicit the generators of the Lie subalgebra $\mathfrak{L}$ in the Dynkin case.

papers.title: G-radical-square-zero algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first provide necessary and sufficient conditions for a Krull-Schmidt triangulated category with Auslander-Reiten triangles to have square-zero radical. One of these conditions is that the middle term of every Auslander-Reiten triangle is either zero or indecomposable. We then call an artin algebra {\it G-radical-square-zero} if the stable category of Gorenstein-projective modules has square-zero radical. We characterize when a G-radical-square-zero algebra is CM-finite and, in this case, give an additive generator of the stable category. For certain Iwanaga-Gorenstein G-radical-square-zero algebras, we further show that the stable category admits an additive generator consisting of higher syzygies of simple modules.

papers.title: Gorenstein dimensions for stable Auslander algebras of Nakayama algebras
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a Nakayama algebra and $\underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A)$ its stable Auslander algebra. We introduce a new homological invariant, called the finitistic Gorenstein dimension, which coincides with the classical Gorenstein dimension whenever the latter is finite, and compute this invariant for $\underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A)$ when $A$ has infinite global dimension. Combined with an accompanying criterion for the finiteness of the Gorenstein dimension of $\underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A)$, our results provide a complete description of this dimension and verify the Gorenstein Symmetry Conjecture for this class of algebras. Furthermore, we show that the finitistic Gorenstein dimension of $ \underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A) $ is also left-right symmetric, is explicitly related to the finitistic dimension of $A$, and can be attained among the injective dimensions of the projective $ \underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A) $-modules corresponding to simple $A$-modules. Our proofs rely on computing injective dimensions in terms of distances in the coresolution forest of $A$, a combinatorial structure closely related to Ringel's coresolution quiver.

papers.title: Gromov-Witten Nonvanishing and Symplectic Deformations of Toric Varieties
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be nonzero in the cohomology ring of a smooth projective toric variety $X$. In this note, we observe the existence of a nonzero Gromov-Witten invariant of the form $\langle A, A, \ldots\rangle_{0, n,\beta}^X$ as a consequence of Iritani's work on the big quantum cohomology ring of $X$. This implies Koll\'ar's conjecture on the symplectic deformation invariance of rational connectedness in the case where $X$ is toric. If $X$ is moreover Fano and $B$ is also nonzero in the cohomology ring, we prove the existence of a nonzero Gromov-Witten invariant of the form $\langle A,B,*\rangle_{0,3,\beta}^X$ using Batyrev's presentation of the small quantum cohomology ring of $X$. We conclude with a few consequences of this nonvanishing result.

papers.title: Hamiltonian GKM spaces via Gromov-Witten theory
papers.abstract:
We use equivariant Gromov-Witten theory to prove the generalised symplectic Mukai inequality for Hamiltonian GKM spaces with large pseudoindex or a special vertex, including smooth Schubert varieties. We also classify all Hamiltonian GKM graphs when the pseudoindex is at least the complex dimension, obtaining a Hamiltonian GKM analogue of the classical Kobayashi-Ochiai classification of complex projective space and complex quadrics.
  Of independent interest are our connectivity theorem for a low-magnitude subgraph of the GKM graph (reminiscent of Campana and Koll\'ar-Miyaoka-Mori's rational chain connectedness of Fano manifolds), and a local Mukai-type theorem that applies at each vertex. We obtain corollaries on reflexive Delzant polytopes that are purely combinatorial in nature.

papers.title: High degree covers and genericity
papers.abstract:
It is known that the genuine irreducible Iwahori-spherical representations of a tame $n$-fold Brylinski-Deligne cover of a $p$-adic split connected reductive group are all generic, when the degree $n$ is suitably large. This has been established by studying the the structure of the Gelfand-Graev representation as a module under the action of the Iwahori-Hecke algebra.
  In this paper, we present a different proof based on metaplectic Moy-Prasad theory.

papers.title: Ideal generation for general reduced projective points
papers.abstract: We prove the Ideal Generation Conjecture for general reduced points in projective space over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Equivalently, if the ideal of the points has initial degree D, multiplication by linear forms from degree D to degree D + 1 has maximal rank. The proof combines hyperplane specialization with a construction using two transverse hyperplanes. In the latter construction, motion of their common trace gives the required rank. A uniform induction for all degrees D ≥ 4 reduces the theorem to explicit quadratic and cubic constructions.

papers.title: Integral torus partition functions just above c=1 have no fixed spectral gap
papers.abstract: We consider modular-invariant torus partition functions of central charge $c>1$ that have a unique vacuum, an expansion in non-degenerate Virasoro characters with positive integer multiplicities, integer spins, no nonvacuum state at the unitarity bound, and parity symmetry. We prove that for every $g>0$ there is $\epsilon(g)>0$ such that no such partition function with $1<c<1+\epsilon(g)$ has all nonvacuum primary dimensions at least $g$. Thus the spectral gap closes as $c\to 1^+$ in this class, as suggested by the numerical bootstrap study of Benjamin, Langhoff, Li and Thaler. The proof is by contradiction and compactness. Using the crystalline-measure reduction of Eberhardt and Levine, we show that every limit at $c=1$ is an equal-weight average of two compact-boson partition functions, at least one at a half-integer radius. Positive Gaussian test functions adapted to the two circle lattices then force every state of a nearby partition function, through a logarithmically growing energy window, to lie within a power of $c-1$ of a lattice point. On the other hand, the central-charge shift of the vacuum contributes a second-order term at zero momentum that no distribution supported on circle lattices and compatible with modular invariance can carry; a finite family of Gaussian tests detects this. Limits with two half-integer radii, where lattice points collide, require a separate analysis. The threshold $\epsilon(g)$ is not effective; we describe the additional estimates that would make it so.

papers.title: Irrationality and Noether--Lefschetz loci in the moduli space of K3 surfaces
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is twofold. First, we construct examples of families of surfaces where the locus of points in the base with constant degree of irrationality is not constructible. Second, we explore the notion of gonality loci in the moduli space of K3 surfaces, which are characterized by the existence of a smooth curve with fixed gonality. Among various results, we prove that polarized gonality loci are always unions of Noether--Lefschetz divisors.

papers.title: Irrationality of χ₂ and Ti₂ at units of real quadratic fields
papers.abstract: We prove that $\chi_2(\sqrt{m^2+1}-m)$, a value of Legendre's chi function at a unit of norm $-1$, is irrational for every integer $m\ge2$ except $m=3,5,7,9,15$. For $m=2$ this shows that $\pi^2-18\log^2\varphi$ is irrational, where $\varphi$ is the golden ratio. The method extends to all units of norm $-1$ in real quadratic fields, giving $\chi_2(\varepsilon)\notin\mathbb{Q}$ outside an explicit set of $47$ units, and, through a twist identity, to the inverse tangent integral $\mathrm{Ti}_2$ at units of norm $+1$, outside $57$ units. The proof combines Hankel determinants of a reflection-symmetric Padé machine, arithmetic bounds on their denominators, a discrete log-gas bound certified in interval arithmetic, and a nonvanishing argument modulo a prime. Below the range covered by the criteria of David, Hirata-Kohno and Kawashima, these results appear to be new. All three theorems are formalised in Lean 4 with Mathlib, using only the standard axioms.

papers.title: Koszul duality and determinant formulas for affine hyperplane arrangements
papers.abstract: For real affine hyperplane arrangements, we prove Lam's determinant conjecture for the inverse Varchenko matrix restricted to bounded chambers. The proof combines Lam's comparison of twisted intersection forms with the period determinant formula of Varchenko, Loeser-Sabbah and Douai-Terao. For normal crossing arrangements, we introduce the taut path algebra and the chamber intersection algebra and establish a Koszul duality between them, yielding an explicit multivariate formula for the inverse Varchenko matrix. After specializing the parameters to $q$, its restriction to bounded chambers is a scalar multiple of the $q$-intersection matrix, proving a determinant conjecture of the authors. We also discuss how the Koszul duality results generalize to affine oriented matroids.

papers.title: Local Rigidity of Bergman Logarithmic Flatness on Compact Hermitian Symmetric Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove the local rigidity of Bergman logarithmic flatness near the standard metrics associated with fixed invariant positive polarizations on compact Hermitian symmetric spaces. Every sufficiently small smooth deformation preserving Bergman logarithmic flatness is induced by a holomorphic automorphism and a constant rescaling. This establishes a Bergman analogue of the local rigidity results for Szeg\H{o} logarithmic flatness obtained by Lu--Tian (Duke Math. J., 2004) and, more recently, Loi--Palmieri--Zuddas (2026).

papers.title: Loops and mirrors
papers.abstract: For a smooth affine complex variety X we construct a Q-algebra LH(X), loop cohomology, in terms of the formal-loop space of X. We conjecture that it is isomorphic to the symplectic cohomology of X. The degree-zero loop cohomology subalgebra is finitely generated for polarized log Calabi-Yau X, constructing an intrinsic mirror affine coordinate ring. Its polyvector algebra is identified with the full loop cohomology algebra for a positive log Calabi-Yau pair with maximal boundary and smooth loop mirror, proving a form of mirror symmetry. In this case we further identify the degree-zero loop cohomology algebra with the Gross-Siebert intrinsic mirror algebra. Assuming in addition that X is a surface, we prove that the full loop and symplectic cohomology algebras agree.

papers.title: Mirror symmetry for gCICY threefolds (I): a $[3,-1]$ block and a non-Gorenstein toric phase
papers.abstract: We construct and analyze a mirror family for the generalized complete intersection Calabi-Yau threefold $X_+=[\mathbb{P}^1\,|\,3\ {-1};\ \mathbb{P}^4\,|\,2\ 3]$, with $(h^{1,1},h^{2,1})=(2,46)$. We introduce auxiliary variables to obtain a toric GIT presentation with two chambers. The first gives $X_+$, while the second gives a Calabi-Yau threefold $X_-$ related to $X_+$ by a flop of 16 disjoint $(-1,-1)$-curves. The threefold $X_-$ is a nef complete intersection in a non-Gorenstein toric $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano eightfold. Then the Hori-Vafa equations give a 2-parameter Laurent family, and we construct a smooth projective crepant model $Y$ of its general member with mirrored Hodge numbers. The rank-6 Picard-Fuchs system of $Y$ has two maximally unipotent boundary points, whose indicial algebras are isomorphic to the even cohomology rings $H^{\mathrm{even}}(X_+,\mathbb{C})$ and $H^{\mathrm{even}}(X_-,\mathbb{C})$. We also show that the predicted genus-zero BPS numbers of the first two vertical degrees agree with direct counts of lines and conics on the genus-one fibration $X_-\to\mathbb{P}^2$.

papers.title: Monodromy and vanishing cycles for complete intersection curves
papers.abstract: We compute the topological monodromy of every family of complete intersection curves. Like in the case of plane curves previously treated by the second-named author, we find the answer is given by the $r$-spin mapping class group associated to the maximal root of the adjoint line bundle. Our main innovation is a suite of tools for studying the monodromy of sections of a tensor product of very ample line bundles in terms of the monodromy of sections of the factors, allowing for an induction on (multi-)degree.

papers.title: Multivariate diagonal harmonics: character polynomials and proofs of two conjectures of Bergeron
papers.abstract:
We prove Bergeron's Hook-Components and Coefficient-Length conjectures for the Vandermonde polarization module and full diagonal harmonics in every rank and number of alphabets. Hook-label characters are elementary skewings of the alternating character, and the maximal Schur length in label $\mu$ is $n-\mu_1$. We compute character and dimension polynomials of diagonal coinvariants in every bosonic--fermionic superspace for $D\ge3$, $n\ge\max\{D,2D-6\}$, answering Church--Ellenberg--Farb's character and dimension questions.
  For augmented commutative algebras in characteristic zero, we construct natural two-Schur presentations and filtered free resolutions with one Schur generator in each homological degree. For polynomial algebras, specialization to orthogonal idempotents identifies the first unstable correction for every nonempty tail $\tau$ and degree $D>|\tau|$. The stable threshold $n\ge D+\tau_1$ is sharp when the row dimension is at least $\ell(\tau)$. First parabolic algebras recover finite jets, their multiplication and their maps.
  Selected-label lifts give uniform Vandermonde generation through degree $D$ for $D\ge3$, $n\ge2D-3$, and disjoint-label products generate every first occurrence for positive integral row weights. Constructive degree reflection determines all two-column moment homology and generates its first syzygies from degree $n+1$; two-column Vandermonde generation reduces to degree $n-1$. Invariants and harmonics separate through the character range and through degree $n$ in two alphabets. The hook identities also give the fully graded sign component of the $t=0$, $(1,2)$-superspace Theta conjecture.

papers.title: Newton non-degenerate holomorphic foliations and their separatrices
papers.abstract: In this paper we study germs of holomorphic foliations in the complex plane that are Newton non-degenerate. This is an algebraic condition attached to the Newton polygon of the foliation, analogous to the one defined by Kouchnirenko for analytic curves and, more generally, hypersurfaces. As in this case, the condition of Newton non-degeneracy for foliations can be identified through the comparison of two numerical invariants: the Newton number - a computation involving simple geometric data of the Newton polygon - and the Milnor number. The Newton number is never greater than the Milnor number, and the foliation is Newton non-degenerate if and only if they are equal. The assumption that a foliation is Newton non-degenerate imposes conditions on its set of separatrices. We prove that, under this hypothesis, the foliation has no weak separatrices and, hence, all its separatrices are analytic. We also give a description of the set of separatrices of a Newton non-degenerate foliation, which is sufficient to characterize the foliation as Newton non-degenerate when it is of generalized curve type. This allows us to prove that the property of being Newton non-degenerate is topologically invariant for foliations of generalized curve type.

papers.title: Non-closed products in branch and weakly branch groups
papers.abstract: We prove that the first Grigorchuk group and the Gupta-Sidki $3$-group are not double coset separable, disproving a conjecture of Grigorchuk, Leemann and Nagnibeda. More generally, every finitely generated regular branch group with bounded activity contains two finitely generated, profinitely closed subgroups with trivial intersection whose product is not closed. Every infinite finitely generated subgroup of the first Grigorchuk group or the Gupta-Sidki $3$-group also fails to be double coset separable. We extend the construction to the $p$-Basilica groups and, using polynomial activity, to the long-range group, whose derived subgroup we prove to be finitely generated. Under an additional hypothesis on finite quotients, we determine the closure of the product. Membership in the constructed product is decidable in the first Grigorchuk group.

papers.title: Non-perpendicular periodic orbits in mirror directions of right triangles
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be a right triangle with an acute angle $a$. A direction is a mirror direction of $T$ if it is the axis of a reflection in the group generated by the reflections in the sides of $T$ — for instance, any direction parallel or perpendicular to a side. A billiard path that meets a side at a right angle retraces itself, its directions are mirror directions, and it is periodic as soon as it meets a side at a right angle a second time. We ask whether every periodic billiard path in a mirror direction is of this kind. When $\cos 2a$ is transcendental it is: every such path meets a side at a right angle, and in the directions parallel to the hypotenuse there is no periodic path at all. The proof is a holonomy computation on Hooper's chain of rhombi, and it bounds the degree of $\cos 2a$ for any exception. When $\cos 2a$ is algebraic and $a/\pi$ irrational, exceptions can occur: we construct non-perpendicular periodic cylinders in mirror directions explicitly — among them an infinite family indexed by the solutions of $u^2 - 2v^2 = -1$ — and show that the triangles carrying them form a countable dense set in each of the four classes of mirror directions. Corollaries include the absence of odd-period orbits in right triangles and the existence of one-way periodic paths in every right triangle (answering two questions of Holt), a description of the odd orbits of isosceles triangles, and the statement that Ruijgrok's third conjecture, read for right triangles, fails on a countable dense set of triangles, all with $\cos 2a$ algebraic, and holds whenever $\cos 2a$ is transcendental.

papers.title: Notes on Wasserstein distance and the JT gravitational ensemble
papers.abstract: This note completes the study of the Boltzmann–Wasserstein (BW) distance, an optimal-transport metric on quantum theories, begun in a companion paper (arXiv:2606.01296). There the distance was evaluated between macroscopically different theories; here we take the opposite limit, two independent draws of the JT-gravity ensemble, which are identical at the classical level. The distance is computable and is controlled by the connected spectral form factor: the ramp, the double-trumpet wormhole, regulated by the plateau, the spectral discreteness. The mean is exponentially small, $\langle \mathcal{W}^2\rangle \sim S_0\, e^{-S_0}$, whereas uncorrelated (Poisson) levels would give an unsuppressed $O(1)$ distance: the self-distance is a sharp diagnostic of spectral chaos. As a metric, the BW distance renders the ensemble a point cloud: exponentially small, strongly anisotropic, its leading principal axis a coherent “breathing” deformation of the low-energy spectrum. Its effective dimension grows asymptotically as $D_{\mathrm{eff}} \simeq 0.42\, S_0^2$, so the distance self-averages, its relative width shrinking as $\mathrm{std}/\mathrm{mean} \sim 1/S_0$. At low temperatures it localizes on the Airy edge, where a single Tracy–Widom mode dominates and self-averaging fails. We test the picture with exact-diagonalization GUE and SYK simulations: in GUE the effective dimension grows logarithmically at every temperature and is predicted at finite $N$, with no free parameters, by the same covariance; unfolded SYK exhibits the predicted anisotropy and mode structure of the cloud. Together with the companion result, this fixes the resolution of the metric: the microstate rigidity computed here is the noise floor beneath a macroscopic difference between theories.

papers.title: On Algebraic LNE models of complex affine algebraic curves
papers.abstract: We give a sufficient condition for an affine complex curve to have an algebraic complex LNE model.

papers.title: On Poincar\'e-Type Inequalities for Flags of Distributions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish enumerative formulas and derive geometric inequalities for flags of holomorphic distributions on complex manifolds. First, given a codimension-one holomorphic distribution $\mathcal{G}$ on a complex manifold $M$, we establish an upper bound for the number of independent holomorphic $p$-distributions tangent to $\mathcal{G}$ with a prescribed associated twisting line bundle $\mathcal{L}$. As an application, we prove Poincar\'e-type degree inequalities for flags on certain classes of manifolds. Finally, we investigate the Mumford--Takemoto stability of the tangent sheaves of rank-two distributions. In particular, we establish several stability results for such distributions on projective spaces, smooth weighted complete intersection threefolds, and, in particular, on smooth hypersurfaces $V\subset\mathbb{P}^4$.

papers.title: On the number of zeros of polyanalytic polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove that a complex polynomial $f(z,\bar z)$ of degree $n$ in $z$ and degree $m<n$ in $\bar{z}$, with finitely many zeros, has at most $(4m+1)n-5m$ distinct zeros in $\mathbb{C}$. The proof uses an approach suggested by GPT-6.1 based on a topological result of Kronheimer and Mrowka (Thom's Conjecture). We provide examples showing that the bound is asymptotically sharp as $n\to\infty$ for each fixed $m$.

papers.title: On the stable birational type of Fano threefolds
papers.abstract: We show that, given a very general cubic threefold $X$, any smooth cubic threefold stably birational to $X$ must be isomorphic to $X$. The method applies as well to other Fano 3-folds, like the sextic double solid, and the quartic threefold. We also discuss the higher-dimensional case.

papers.title: On the strong Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence for the quantum semisimple groups
papers.abstract: The Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence, when it holds for an algebra, characterizes its primitive ideals ( that is, the annihilators of irreducible representations) both algebraically and topologically within the prime spectrum. A stronger form, known as the strong Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence, was introduced by Bell, Launois, and Nolan in their work on 'A strong Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence for quantum Schubert cells'. In this paper, we prove that the generic quantized coordinate rings of connected, simply connected semisimple complex algebraic groups satisfy the strong Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence.

papers.title: On the symplectic cohomology of orbifold divisor complements
papers.abstract: This article studies the symplectic cohomology of Liouville domains whose contact boundaries admit a periodic Reeb flow, with a particular focus on affine varieties which arise as orbifold divisor complements. We describe a computation of the transverse Conley-Zehnder indices which allows for a simple computation of the positive equivariant symplectic cohomology in cases when the inertia orbifold of the compactifying divisor has only even cohomology. This is then applied to the classification of orbifold compactifications of $\mathbb{C}^n$. Moreover, we study the action of multiplication by the principal orbit on V-shaped symplectic cohomology and prove that if the compactification $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{D})$ is positively monotone, then this class induces a periodic structure on symplectic cohomology, reducing the problem of computing an infinite-dimensional group to a finite-dimensional repeating portion. We combine the index computations and this periodic structure to compute the symplectic cohomology of various Milnor fibers of surface singularities, the rational homology balls $B_{p,1}$ as well as complements of star-shaped configurations of rational curves in K3 surfaces, which includes the Milnor fibers of the exceptional unimodal singularities.

papers.title: On the topology of some linear systems of hyperelliptic curves in Hirzebruch surfaces
papers.abstract: Following a program suggested by Dolgachev and Libgober in 1981, we study the topology of the locus of smooth sections of linear systems of hyperelliptic curves on Hirzebruch surfaces. Our primary interest is the computation of various flavors of ``enriched monodromy representations''. Within this class of examples, we find that a variety of behaviors occur - in some situations the enriched monodromy faithfully captures the fundamental group, and in others it does not. Our arguments mainly leverage algebro-geometric techniques to compute cohomological obstructions to families of embeddings.

papers.title: On the volume of K-semistable Fano manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that the anti-canonical volume of an $n$-dimensional K-semistable Fano manifold that is not $\mathbb{P}^n$ is at most $2n^n$. Moreover, the volume is equal to $2n^n$ if and only if $X\cong \mathbb{P}^1\times \mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ or $X$ is a smooth quadric hypersurface $Q\subset \mathbb{P}^{n+1}$. Our proof is based on a new connection between K-semistability and minimal rational curves.

papers.title: Ostrik's Theorem for Operator Algebras in a Unitary Tensor Category
papers.abstract: We define Hilbert modules for $\mathrm{C^*}$ and $\mathrm{W^*}$ algebra objects in the ind-completion of a unitary tensor category. We then prove an operator algebraic Ostrik's theorem in an ind-category: the 2-category of $\mathrm{C^*}$ or $\mathrm{W^*}$ algebras objects, their modules, and adjointable intertwiners is $\dagger$-equivalent to the 2-categories of $\mathrm{C^*}$ or $\mathrm{W^*}$ module categories.

papers.title: Override and Update in Restriction Categories
papers.abstract: We study the override and update operators on partial functions from the perspective of restriction categories. We propose a definition of override restriction categories, in which both of the operators in question exist. We prove a number of results concerning these operators and their relationship to the structure of the ambient restriction category, as well as relating them to the existing literature on the override and update operators. We provide various examples of override restriction categories and in particular show that every classical restriction category is an override restriction category.

papers.title: Palindromic sections in two Kolakoski phase actions
papers.abstract: We prove the two specified-phase orbit statements in Shen's Conjectures 3.4 and 3.7. The all-ones phase for the alphabet $\{1,n\}$, with $n$ positive and even, and both alternating phases for $\{-1,n\}$, with $n$ any even integer, have orbit length $2^{\lceil d/2\rceil}$ at depth $d$. The proof uses unreduced signed words and a palindrome class preserved by taking the section of the square at two phase coordinates. It also gives the all-ones statement for nonpositive even $n$ under Shen's displayed signed recursion. These are finite phase-orbit results; they do not imply the density conjecture for the classical Kolakoski sequence.

papers.title: Parabolic induction and pullback of perverse sheaves on Vogan varieties
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a Levi subgroup of a quasisplit connected reductive group $G$ over a $p$-adic field. Vogan's geometric perspective on the local Langlands correspondence fixes a perfect pairing between the Grothendieck group of representations of $G$ and its pure inner forms with a fixed infinitesimal parameter and the Grothendieck group of equivariant perverse sheaves on the associated Vogan variety. Granting a list of desiderata for the enhanced local Langlands correspondence, we show that parabolic induction $\mathrm{Ind}_M^G$ is the transpose of geometric restriction $\xi^*$ with respect to this pairing if and only if the $p$-adic analogue of the Kazhdan--Lusztig hypothesis and the expected multiplicity formula for tempered induction both hold. The identity refines to one for each pure inner form of $G$.

papers.title: Parabolic semiinfinite sheaves on affine flag varieties
papers.abstract: We study sheaves on affine flag varieties of reductive algebraic groups in parabolic semiinfinite settings, generalizing some constructions and results from the work of Gaitsgory and of Achar, Dhillon, and the first author (for the case of the Borel subgroup) and of Dhillon and Lysenko (for characteristic-$0$ coefficients and a particular case of parabolic semiinfinite condition). In particular we define perverse t-structures and Raskin equivalences in this context, and study an analogue of the Gaitsgory sheaf. In future work, these $\infty$-categories will be related to representation-theoretic $\infty$-categories associated with the Langlands dual group.

papers.title: Pellarin's Identity, Carlitz Period, and Anderson Generating Functions over Arbitrary Curves
papers.abstract: We establish three results for a rank-one Drinfeld module over the coefficient ring of a smooth, projective, geometrically connected curve over $ \mathbb F_q$, with a closed point at infinity of arbitrary degree. First, a Tate-algebra unit exists in the module of special functions precisely when this module is free of rank one, that is, when the period lattice is isomorphic to the module of regular differentials; this proves the Gazda--Maurischat conjecture. Second, under the unit-anchor normalization for an isogeny to a principal-period target, a strictly normalized shtuka product and one characteristic residue give the fundamental period; the same defect equation gives the logarithm residue formula. Third, finite \'{e}tale torsion traces over the field of definition identify the first Frobenius twist of the normalized shtuka differential and express Pellarin's $ \mathcal L(1)$-series at a fundamental period. The source period lattice need not be free.

papers.title: Periods and CM motives of abelian type
papers.abstract: We associate algebraic Hecke characters to certain invertible motives for absolute Hodge cycles with coefficients in a number field $K$, reversing a viewpoint of Schappacher. These motives $N$ include abelian motives and a new notion of algebraic motive. This Hecke character determines the complex and the $p$-adic periods of $N$, and is determined by the latter; this gives a proof of the Mumford-Tate conjecture for $N$. When $K$ and $N$ are abelian, we prove a refinement of the Gross-Deligne conjecture, as well as $l$-adic and $p$-adic variants. We also formulate a version of the algebraic relations between rational values of the gamma function given by Koblitz and Ogus in terms of a distribution with values in the Picard group of the category of (abelian) Chow motives.

papers.title: Positive bases and polytopes for Laurent phenomenon algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that the cluster monomials of every graph Laurent phenomenon algebra form an atomic positive basis. For every finite normalized Laurent phenomenon algebra over a unique factorization domain, we construct a simple lattice polytope with unimodular normal fan whose polar realizes the cluster complex. We also prove that cluster monomials form a basis of the upper algebra in the finite case. In particular, every linear Laurent phenomenon algebra admits such a polyhedral realization.

papers.title: Positivity for Weighted Linear Laurent Phenomenon Algebras
papers.abstract: We prove Laurent positivity for ordinary Laurent phenomenon algebras whose initial exchange polynomials are nonconstant affine linear polynomials with positive constant terms and nonnegative numerical coefficients.

papers.title: Projective Variety Recovery from Unknown Linear Projections
papers.abstract: We study how a smooth irreducible variety $X$ of dimension $n$ and degree $d$ in $\mathbb{P}^m$, $m\geq n+2$, can be recovered from the equations of its images under two generic projections from unknown centers. This extends earlier results on curves in $\mathbb{P}^3$ and surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^4$ to any dimension. Since $X$ is the normalization of each image, one image determines $X$ modulo the projective group when $X$ is linearly normal; what two images add is the configuration, that is the pair of projections. For complete intersections we prove unconditionally that the set of configurations compatible with the two images and their Hilbert polynomial is finite, of size at most $|\mathrm{Lin}(X)|$, the projective automorphism group of $X$. The argument is effective and the bound is attained. We then introduce an equation generalizing Kruppa's equation, relating the duals of the images to a fundamental matrix, encoding the pair of projections modulo the projective group. We give a necessary condition for its solution variety to be finite, a bound on its isolated points, and a sufficient condition under which the true fundamental matrix is rigid: no quadric may contain a generic line $L$ together with the locus of points of $X$ whose tangent space meets $L$. Rigidity is unconditional for curves; in higher dimension it holds under a first-order liftability hypothesis, which we certify for a del Pezzo quartic surface in $\mathbb{P}^4$. Global finiteness of that solution variety remains open, necessarily so, as it contains solutions realized by no variety; for $\dim X<\mathrm{codim}\,X-1$ the obstruction amounts to knowing the fundamental matrix itself. Once the projections are known, $X$ is recovered from the two cones over the images: in codimension two their intersection is $X$ plus a component of degree $d(d-1)$; in higher codimension $X$ is its unique component of maximal dimension.

papers.title: Quantum Langlands correspondence for Painlev\'e II
papers.abstract: We construct an irregular KZ-BPZ correspondence for quantum Painlev\'e II from a rank-three Wakimoto-Whittaker module. The irregular KZ equation and the quantum isomonodromy equation form a joint affine system whose Drinfeld-Sokolov reduction yields scalar BPZ equations. We obtain matrix-integral solutions of this system for one fundamental insertion. An exact quantum Langlands duality exchanges the fundamental insertion with the zero of the dual Whittaker differential and allows affine solutions to be reconstructed from the BPZ equations. This duality interchanges the classical and Nekrasov-Shatashvili limits, which yield the Painlev\'e II Lax connection and an irregular Gaudin oper, respectively.

papers.title: Quartic exponential matching in the unit square
papers.abstract: Take two independent samples of $n$ uniform points in the unit square. We prove that, with probability at least one half, the points can be paired so that the average of the exponential of the fourth power of the normalized pair distance is at most two. The distance normalization is $L\sqrt{\log n/n}$, with $L$ an absolute constant. One pairing therefore satisfies both coordinate inequalities in the symmetric $(4,4)$ case of Talagrand's matching problem. The argument first controls a vector field transporting smoothed point densities, and then converts that control to a pairing. The main estimate comes from a Gaussian construction whose successive partitions depend only on noise already revealed; a correction using the classical bottleneck matching preserves the required density balance.

papers.title: Ramification of torsion packets on curves with good-reduction Jacobians
papers.abstract: Let $p\ge5$ be a prime number, $k$ an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$. Write $R=W(k)$ for the ring of Witt vectors over $k$, and $K$ for the field of fractions of $R$. Let $X$ be a smooth, proper, geometrically connected curve over $K$ of genus greater than one. Write $J$ for the Jacobian variety of $X$. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{K}$ of $K$. In the present paper, we prove that if $J$ has good reduction over $R$, then every point $x\in X(\overline{K})$ such that $[\sigma x-x]$ is torsion for each $\sigma\in \operatorname{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)$ is $K$-rational.

papers.title: Rank Additivity and Comon's Conjecture for Real Hankel Tensors
papers.abstract: Let $\mathscr{H}_m(n)$ denote the set of real Hankel tensors of order $m$ and dimension $n$, and let $\textbf{H}\in\mathscr{H}_m(n)$, where $m\ge3$ and $n\ge1$. Set $M=(m-1)(n-1)+1$. First, we prove that the CP rank $r(\textbf{H})\le M$ and that CP rank is additive under direct sums of $\textbf{H}$ with any real tensor $\textbf{T}$ of the same order. Second, we prove that partially symmetric rank $p_j(\textbf{H})=r(\textbf{H})$ for $1\le j\le m-1$ and that, if $r(\textbf{H})\le M-1$, these ranks also equal its symmetric rank $s(\textbf{H})$. Third, we construct a fourth-order Hankel tensor $\textbf{H}_*\in\mathscr{H}_4(4)$ that attains this CP rank bound and satisfies $r(\textbf{H}_*)=10$ and $s(\textbf{H}_*)=11$. Moreover, for the direct sum $\textbf{H}_*^{(k)}=\bigoplus_{a=1}^k\textbf{H}_*$, we further prove that $r(\textbf{H}_*^{(k)})=10k$ and $s(\textbf{H}_*^{(k)})=11k$. This provides a low-dimensional counterexample to Comon's conjecture over the real numbers and further shows that the Comon rank gap is unbounded among real symmetric tensors of order four.

papers.title: Reciprocal mirror map derivatives, euler-twisted Gromov-Witten invariants, and instanton counts via quantum Serre duality
papers.abstract: We study mirror map derivatives as a means of relating the genus zero Gromov-Witten theories of an anticanonical Calabi-Yau hypersurface in a smooth, almost minimal Fano variety and the local Calabi-Yau formed from the total space of the Fano's canonical bundle with the euler-twisted theory of the ambient Fano.
