A precise relationship between reciprocal mirror map derivatives is obtained from the non-equivariant limit of quantum Serre duality for the euler-twisted theory of the ambient Fano as formulated by Iritani, Mann, & Mignon. This allows us to express the generating series of 3-point euler-twisted invariants as the derivative of the local mirror map with respect to the closed one. In low dimensions, this series is shown to be a modular form of Eisenstein type which has arisen before in this area. We prove integrality of the twisted invariants from this identification. The regularized small quantum $D$-module of the Fano is reducible, and we show it is equivalent to an inhomogeneous Picard-Fuchs equation governed by this generating series. The reciprocal mirror map derivative is then shown to be a generating function of local 3-point invariants, which recovers some known results for local Calabi-Yau threefolds and proves a conjecture of the second named author and A. Malmendier in previous work on local fourfolds. Explicit calculations for $\mathbb{P}^2,\mathbb{P}^3$ and $\mathbb{P}^4$ illustrate these relationships, which includes the vanishing of positive-degree ordinary genus-zero invariants for anticanonical elliptic curves and K3 surfaces, the recovery of the quintic threefold's instanton numbers, and finally some formulas for genus-zero invariants of local projective spaces.

papers.title: Regular loci of affine Springer fibers at very special parahoric level
papers.abstract: For split groups, we prove that centralizers act transitively on regular loci of affine Springer fibers at very special parahoric level. As an application, we prove Chi's conjecture on the number of top-dimensional irreducible components of affine Lusztig varieties.

papers.title: Representations of the Loop mirror BMS-Kac-Moody algebra
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct a new family of non-weight modules $\Omega(\lambda,\zeta,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\sigma, h)$ over the loop mirror BMS-Kac-Moody algebra $\mathcal{G}$, which is a Takiff-type extension of the loop mirror Heisenberg--Virasoro algebra. We establish criteria for irreducibility, determine their isomorphism classes, and classify all $\mathcal{G}$-modules that are free of rank one. Moreover, we determine all self-extensions of these modules: for every such module $M$, $\operatorname{Ext}^{1}_{U(\mathcal{G})}(M,M)\cong \mathbb{C}^{6}$, and we construct explicit $1$-cocycles realizing every cohomology class. Every nonsplit self-extension of a simple module is indecomposable of composition length two. Restricting these modules to the loop mirror Heisenberg--Virasoro subalgebra $\mathcal{H}$ yields new $\mathcal{H}$-modules. Among them the $\sigma$-type modules $\Psi(\lambda,\zeta,\sigma,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,h)$ constitute a new family with no counterpart in the non-loop or non-Takiff case. For the degenerate case $\sigma=0$, we establish criteria for irreducibility and isomorphism, and describe certain maximal submodules and their simple quotients. Finally, we construct and classify a new class of tensor product $\mathcal{H}$-modules.

papers.title: Shifted Lagrangian structures and syzygies on Calabi--Yau varieties
papers.abstract: In \cite{FMR25}, Fantechi--Mir\'o-Roig show how to construct new Lagrangian subspaces of the moduli of simple perfect sheaves on a K3 surface from a given one. We reinterpret their construction using the tools and flexibility of derived algebraic geometry. This allows us to generalize from K3 surfaces to (possibly singular) Calabi--Yau schemes of arbitrary dimensions.

papers.title: Singular perpendicular orbits and complete periodicity in rational triangles
papers.abstract: Let $\Delta$ be a triangle whose angles are rational multiples of $\pi$. A billiard path leaving a side $\sigma$ at a right angle either meets a vertex first — its starting point is then singular — or meets a side at a right angle again: $\sigma$ itself, at a new point, or another side, where it retraces itself. The singular points cut $\sigma$ into finitely many intervals, and each interval retraces or is carried onto another by the return map, reversing orientation (a mirror pair) or preserving it (a translation pair). We count these intervals exactly. The singular points of the sides perpendicular to a direction class are in bijection with the slots — a vertex with a direction of the class pointing inward — whose path meets a side at a right angle before any vertex, so the number of intervals is $v + S - 2p - s'$: $S$ slots, $v$ perpendicular sides, $p$ pairs of mutually reverse vertex-to-vertex paths meeting no side at a right angle, and $s'$ slots whose path never reaches a vertex. This bounds the retracing bands and translation pairs, sharply on isosceles triangles, and makes $s' = 0$ equivalent to complete periodicity of the class. Our main theorem is that $p = 0$ forces complete periodicity: a minimal component needs a swapped pair. The converse fails. In every isosceles triangle $(a, a, b)$ with $N$ even and $a \geq 3$ the class of the base direction has $p \geq 1$, and it is completely periodic, by a companion paper (computer-assisted in part), whenever $b \geq 4$ and $N$ has at most one odd prime factor. At odd $N$, two infinite families of scalene triangles have $p \geq 1$ and are completely periodic in the checked range.

papers.title: Singular points of envelopes and offsets: a transition from 2D to 3D
papers.abstract: We recall properties of the offsets of a (plane) kiss curve and their singularities, then we make a transition to 3D, considering the surface obtained by revolution of the kiss curve about one of its axes. When pos?sible, geometric constructions using automated methods are performed. This induces a need to focus on algebraic computations. Networking be?tween different kinds of software is of utmost importance, in order to use their respective strengths (dynamic geometry, dragging points, strong al?gebraic computations, etc.). A core difference between the 2D and 3D situations is that automated commands existing in 2D are not available in 3D. This makes the DGS less relevant in 3D than in 2D. In 3D, most of the work must be performed with the CAS. The singular points of a kiss curve in the plane are tacnodes (cusps) and crunodes (self-intersection). The singularities are not isolated anymore and cuspidal edges appear. In this setting, implicitization is a heavy endeavour and we need another technology, related to AI; we describe this briefly. The 2D activities have been proposed to in-service teachers learning towards an advanced degree.

papers.title: Smale's mean value constant (1981) equals 4
papers.abstract: For a complex polynomial p of degree d ≥ 2 with p(0) = 0 and p′(0) ≠ 0, let S(p) be the minimum of |p(c)/(c p′(0))| over the critical points c of p, and let K(d) be the supremum of S(p) over all such p of degree d. In 1981 Smale proved that K(d) ≤ 4 for every d, and asked whether 4 can be replaced by 1. We prove that Smale's mean value constant sup_d K(d) equals 4 and that K(d) → 4 as d → ∞, combining a reduction due to Jatar and Ng with an explicit construction. Each K(d) is known to be below 4, so the supremum is not attained. The main result has also been formalized in the Lean 4 proof assistant.

papers.title: Smale's mean value constant (1981) equals 4, and other miscellanea
papers.abstract: For a complex polynomial p of degree d ≥ 2 with p(0) = 0 and p′(0) ≠ 0, let S(p) be the minimum of |p(c)/(c p′(0))| over the critical points c of p, and let K(d) be the supremum of S(p) over all such p of degree d. In 1981 Smale proved that K(d) ≤ 4 for every d, and asked whether 4 can be replaced by 1. We prove that Smale's mean value constant sup_d K(d) equals 4 and that K(d) → 4 as d → ∞, combining a reduction due to Jatar and Ng with an explicit construction. Each K(d) is known to be below 4, so the supremum is not attained. The main result has also been formalized in the Lean 4 proof assistant. We give three further proofs: by a variant of the main construction in which part of the boundary of an auxiliary domain is a level curve of an entire function; by a Riemann map onto a domain with thin hairs; and by a Riemann surface whose conformal radius at its base point is near 1. We also include a complete proof of the known fact that K(d) does not decrease.

papers.title: Smale's mean value constant (1981) exceeds 1.1559, and other miscellanea
papers.abstract: We prove that Smale's mean value constant exceeds $1.1559837$, improving the bound $1.1018$ of Jatar and Ng; after the first version of this paper, the author proved that it equals $4$. Smale proved in 1981 that for every complex polynomial $P$ of degree at least $2$ and every point $z$ with $P'(z)\neq0$, some critical point $\zeta$ of $P$ satisfies $|P(z)-P(\zeta)|\le K\,|z-\zeta|\,|P'(z)|$ with $K=4$, and he conjectured that $K=1$ suffices; $K^*$ is the best constant, called Smale's mean value constant. That conjecture was disproved in 2026. Jatar and Ng showed that $K^*$ equals the supremum of $1/B(0)$ over the admissible pairs $(W,B)$: $W$ is a normalised univalent map of the unit disk, $B$ is a finite Blaschke product with $B(0)>0$, and the derivative of the product $WB$ has no zero in the disk. We construct such a pair explicitly, with $B$ of degree two, from a polynomial of degree $18$ with Gaussian rational coefficients, and we verify the required properties by a computation in exact arithmetic. Writing $\mathcal B_d$ for this supremum restricted to $\deg B\le d$, we prove, partly with certified computation, that $1.1363375<\mathcal B_1<1.177801$, $\mathcal B_2<100/61$, and $\mathcal B_d\le4-0.00597/(d\log d)$ for every $d\ge2$, which improves the bound of Jatar and Ng for $d\ge452$. If a pair attains $\mathcal B_d$ with $d\ge1$, then $W$ does not extend holomorphically to any neighbourhood of the closed disk and is not rational. If $1/B_n(0)\to4$ along a sequence of admissible pairs $(W_n,B_n)$ (such sequences exist, since $K^*=4$), then after rotation $W_n$ tends to the Koebe function, as Jatar and Ng observed, and the zeros $a$ of $B_n$, weighted by $\log(1/|a|)$, have an explicit limit distribution. Every admissible pair $(W,B)$ with $W$ meromorphic on a neighbourhood of the closed disk has $\deg B\le\operatorname{wt}(W)$, a weighted count of the points of the circle where $|W|$ is stationary and $\arg W$ decreases.

papers.title: Smooth functions with isolated critical values and systems of fibers
papers.abstract: In the 2020s, Marzantowicz and Michalak have introduced the notion of system of smooth hypersurfaces and discussed Morse functions compatible with them: the hypersurfaces are regular level sets of the functions. This is a kind of fundamental theory on Morse functions and related differential topology and geometric topology. We extend this to a certain case: we discuss systems of regular level sets and critical level sets (regular fibers and singular fibers) of smooth functions with isolated critical values.

papers.title: Special Loci in the Moduli of Curves
papers.abstract: We introduce new techniques to study mixed-characteristic special loci in moduli spaces and give several applications, focusing in particular on the moduli space $\mathsf{M}_g$ of curves. These applications include Zariski density results for split Jacobians, non-density results for supersingular loci, and lifting results for algebraic cycles, all under appropriate numerical conditions. Our methods generalize to more-or-less arbitrary moduli spaces mapping to Hodge-type Shimura varieties (and even some settings beyond the Shimura case), and relate to questions raised by Oort and de Jong.

papers.title: Splitting module-finite extensions over singular local rings
papers.abstract: We study when a module-finite extension of a singular local ring splits as a module over the base. On a Gorenstein curve of positive residue characteristic, weak normality forces splitting for every extension of finite projective dimension. In residue characteristic two the converse holds when two is zero or a nonzerodivisor. A missing square root in the prescribed base gives an explicit nonsplit extension of generic rank four. We obtain a second curve criterion by gluing retractions on the branches and determine all evaluation ideals for coordinate crossings and for \(x^2=y^2u z_1\cdots z_s\) in odd characteristic. For cubic extensions we prove a presentation theorem with arbitrarily many relations. It applies on the blow-up of an ideal generated by a regular sequence of length three, and on the blow-up of a three-dimensional local ring with a quadric tangent cone. A family of matrices satisfying the criterion exists over every residue field in the regular-sequence case.

papers.title: Square root crystals and the square root of $B(\infty)$
papers.abstract: We introduce a general monoidal category of $\mathbf{N}$-root crystals and then study the special case of square root $\mathfrak{gl}_n$-crystals. The latter objects include Yu's crystals on semistandard set-valued tableaux. Prior work of the first author, Tong, and Yu showed that regular square root $\mathfrak{gl}_n$-crystals can be a useful tool for proving Grothendieck positivity results. The objects studied here go beyond the regular case and allow us to construct a square root analog of the direct limit crystal $B(\infty)$. We give several descriptions of our square root of $B(\infty)$, using marginally large tableaux, the Lusztig or PBW parameterization, and the Nakashima--Zelevinsky polyhedral model. We show that this crystal has a simple character formula, exhibits a nontrivial Demazure filtration, and recovers Yu's semistandard set-valued tableau crystals after taking appropriate tensor products. We also investigate a number of differences between square root crystals and classical crystal constructions.

papers.title: Stacky geometry and logarithmic topology of transversely affine foliations
papers.abstract: We study the linear monodromy of codimension-one transversely affine foliations through multiplicative quotient stacks and logarithmic boundary topology. When the transverse affine structure admits a global presentation on $U$, a choice of multiplicative developing coordinate induces a morphism to $[\mathbb{C}^*/\Gamma]$, where $\Gamma\subset\mathbb{C}^*$ is the image of the linear monodromy. We prove that for infinite $\Gamma$ every strict semi-equivariant holomorphic self-map of $\mathbb{C}^*$ is a monomial, and classify the nonconstant strict semi-equivariant rational self-maps of $\mathbb{P}^1$ for arbitrary $\Gamma$. For a logarithmic connection along a simple normal crossings divisor, we describe the meridional characters and angular foliations on the boundary fibres of the Kato--Nakayama space, including the topology and closures of their leaves. We also describe the extension of the linear monodromy local system to this space and the effect of local Kummer base change on finite meridional monodromy.

papers.title: Standard modules and Dold--Kan correspondences for generalized Reedy categories
papers.abstract: We develop a representation-theoretic approach to generalized Reedy categories through a systematic study of standard modules. For a broad class of these categories, we provide a uniform, computable framework that reduces abstract Hom-spaces between standard modules to elementary linear algebra and graph theory via incidence matrices and morphism fibers. As a primary application, we establish a uniform extension of the Dold--Kan correspondence for certain categories arising from rooted trees, and obtain an orthogonal decomposition for finite spiders, including the category of finite sets and partial injections. Crucially, this machinery unifies and provides a single conceptual framework for several classical, seemingly disparate results across algebraic topology and representation theory, including Kuhn's decomposition theorem for vector spaces and the Th\'evenaz--Webb semisimplicity theorem for Mackey functors.

papers.title: Stochastic Connections on Surface Bundles
papers.abstract: We construct local stochastic connection dynamics on arbitrary principal bundles over closed oriented Riemannian surfaces. For each smooth reference connection, the bare additive spatial heat approximations of the Yang–Mills–DeTurck equation converge to a maximal local strong Markov family in a separable negative Hölder space. A finite Gaussian enhancement defines the singular products, and cancellation of the total logarithmic mass identifies the limiting equation. Rough comparison gauges and predictable rotations of the Wiener noise identify the local orbit laws for different references. The finite quadratic tensor anomaly vanishes after the two-dimensional Yang–Mills contraction, with the finite normalisation fixed by the spatial heat approximation. Continuing through bounded representatives gives a reference-independent maximal local strong Markov family on the full rough orbit space. Gaussian line primitives have every Hölder exponent below one on bounded regular curve families and define non-Abelian Young parallel transport. On a dense, gauge-invariant Borel full-heat trace domain, polygonal holonomies separate rough gauge orbits, admit Borel representative maps, and recover the bundle class. The orbit dynamics has continuous holonomy paths on this domain, and the regularised holonomies converge uniformly on bounded regular curve families and compact surviving positive-time intervals. We also prove regularisation-independent convergence of first-order Gaussian currents after time integration, including a harmonic example of infinite variation and zero quadratic variation. At fixed regularisation scale, the field-dependent covariant heat approximation has classical solutions and an explicit Itô correction in Coulomb coordinates. In every Abelian sector, the quotient diffusion is global, reference independent, and reversible with an explicitly identified unique invariant law.

papers.title: Sublinear-space recognition for Boolean grammars
papers.abstract: For every fixed Boolean grammar in the standard language family considered by Okhotin, we give a deterministic membership algorithm using $O_G(n^{2/3}(\log(n+2))^{2/3})$ working space on an input of length $n$. In particular, the whole family is contained in $\operatorname{DSPACE}(n^{3/4})$, answering Okhotin's Problem 4 affirmatively. The construction partitions substring endpoints into blocks of size $b$. It represents the parsing recurrence by a constant-fan-in circuit with $O_G(b^2)$-bit values and dependency height $O(n/b+1)$. Splits in the endpoint blocks are resolved locally, and an ordering of the remaining splits controls the height even when a split is highly unbalanced. Applying the Cook–Mertz tree-evaluation algorithm to the implicitly unfolded circuit gives the space bound.

papers.title: The $\mathbb Q$-gonality of $X_1(42)$ is $12$
papers.abstract: We prove that the $\mathbb F_5$-gonality and the $\mathbb Q$-gonality of the modular curve $X_1(42)$ are both $12$, improving the previous lower bound of $10$. Since $J_1(42)(\mathbb Q)$ is finite, it follows that $12$ is the least degree in which $X_1(42)$ has infinitely many points. The lower bound comes from an exhaustive search over Riemann--Roch spaces, following Derickx and van Hoeij, using a new reduction by the orbits of a cyclic group of automorphisms of order $12$ on places of degree at most $5$ ($743\,231$ Riemann--Roch spaces). An earlier search with the reductions from van Hoeij's code (about $3$ million Riemann--Roch spaces, about $6$ times more CPU time) gives the same result and serves as supporting evidence. We prove the reductions and record the data needed to reproduce the computations.

papers.title: The 51-state beeper $M_{51}$: every battle ends, and what Peano Arithmetic can prove about it
papers.abstract: We study an explicit 51-state, 2-symbol beeping Turing machine $M_{51}$ and its associated dispatch-level process $R$. An ordinal descent below $\varepsilon_0$ proves that every battle of $R$ terminates and hence that $M_{51}$ beeps infinitely often. A growth lemma shows that the battle counters and beep times eventually dominate every function provably computable in Peano Arithmetic. Together with a Rocq-checked simulation theorem, these results establish that quasihalting of $M_{51}$ is independent of Peano Arithmetic. The document includes the process definition, machine table, ordinal analysis, growth proof and an account of its external dependencies.

papers.title: The Benson-Etingof-Ostrik conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the conjecture of Benson--Etingof--Ostrik (2023): every symmetric tensor category of moderate growth over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic admits a symmetric tensor functor to a higher Verlinde category, possibly of infinite height. Using maximal nilpotence and geometric reductivity, we reduce the problem to proving that finitely generated maximally nilpotent tensor categories are finite. The main ingredients are the construction of generic points using alternating norms and a Frobenius reduction of the fundamental coend to an ordinary Hopf subalgebra.

papers.title: The Bruce-Roberts Tjurina number of holomorphic 1-forms along complex analytic varieties
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of the \textit{Bruce-Roberts Tjurina number} for holomorphic 1-forms with respect to a pair $(X,V)$ of complex analytic subvarieties. We characterize its finiteness and, when $X$ and $V$ are hypersurfaces with at most isolated singularities, relate it to a determinantal colength, the Tjurina number of the 1-form with respect to $V$, and the Tjurina number of $X$. We also establish a decomposition of the difference between the Bruce-Roberts Milnor and Tjurina numbers and a bound for their quotient. As an application, we prove a relative quasihomogeneity result for germs of non-dicritical generalized curve foliations in complex dimension two.

papers.title: The Cayley-Bedregal reduction for Milnor and Hirzebruch-Milnor classes
papers.abstract:
The Cayley--Bedregal reduction replaces a complete intersection $\{f_1=\dots=f_r=0\}$ by the hypersurface $\sum_i\varphi_if_i=0$ in the projectivized dual bundle. For an isolated complete intersection singularity of corank $c$, we express the Milnor class of this hypersurface on its singular fibre $\mathbb P^{c-1}$ in terms of the Milnor numbers of generic systems obtained by taking linear combinations of the defining equations. Its degree is the original Milnor number, and the higher components recover the Milnor numbers of the systems with fewer equations. These numbers are invariants of the analytic germ.
  Our second main result concerns the Hodge-theoretic refinement. For a complete intersection defined by a regular section of a rank-$r$ algebraic vector bundle, the Hirzebruch--Milnor class is determined by that of the Cayley--Bedregal hypersurface: the push-forward of the normalized Hirzebruch--Milnor class of the hypersurface, in the sense of Cappell, Maxim, Sch\"urmann and Shaneson, is $(-y)^{r-1}$ times that of the complete intersection, with no positivity assumption on the bundle. The factor $(-y)^{r-1}$ comes from the motivic decomposition of the projective bundle, and at $y=-1$ the identity recovers Aluffi's comparison of Milnor classes. When the tautological bundle is very ample, the hypersurface formula of Maxim, Saito and Sch\"urmann then gives the Hirzebruch--Milnor class of the complete intersection through the vanishing cycles of a single function, avoiding their induction through intermediate complete intersections and their restriction to powers of one line bundle. In integral homology we prove the analytic form of Aluffi's identity, and obtain formulas for the Milnor class in terms of local Milnor fibres and for the Chern--Schwartz--MacPherson class of any projective scheme.

papers.title: The commuting scheme of $\mathfrak{g}_2$ and a degree formula for commuting schemes
papers.abstract: Over a field of characteristic zero, we show that the commuting scheme of the exceptional Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}_2$ is Cohen-Macaulay and normal (in particular, reduced). We determine its Hilbert series, show that it has degree $1825$ and is not Gorenstein, and determine an explicit linear system of parameters. A crucial ingredient of (one of) our proofs is a root theoretic formula for the degree of the commuting scheme of any reductive Lie algebra whose Borel subalgebra has a complete-intersection commuting scheme, which includes all classical Lie algebras of small rank as well as $E_6$ and $G_2$. Finally, we give a criterion that implies Cohen-Macaulayness and reducedness of the commuting scheme in any given positive characteristic and use it to show that the commuting scheme is Cohen-Macaulay and reduced for every prime $5\leq p\leq1000$. We also resolve the `bad' characteristic cases and show that the commuting scheme is reduced and Cohen-Macaulay over fields of characteristic $3$, and reduced but not Cohen-Macaulay over fields of characteristic $2$ where it has degree $438$.

papers.title: The Daugavet Property of Bidual Spaces
papers.abstract: We construct a separable Banach space whose bidual has the Daugavet property. The construction proceeds by successively extending finite-dimensional spaces so that prescribed vectors are approximated by averages of newly added unit vectors. A simultaneous extension argument produces finitely many fixed functionals whose norm-attaining faces approximate the unit ball of the bidual.

papers.title: The elliptic Hall algebra and the combinatorics of affine Springer fibers
papers.abstract: For coprime positive integers $m,n$ and $k\ge1$, we study the symmetric functions $e_k[-X^{m,n}Y]\cdot1$ arising from the elliptic Hall algebra action. We identify their $\omega_X$-transforms with the normalized bigraded Frobenius characteristics computed by Boixeda Alvarez--Hameister--Ma for the torus-equivariant Borel--Moore homology of the positive parts of homogeneous affine Springer fibers. We introduce cyclic LLT polynomials and determine their monomial expansions, yielding explicit monomial formulas for these elliptic Hall algebra expressions in terms of cyclic parking functions. These results extend the affine Springer fiber identity and monomial formula of Carlsson--Mellit from integral slopes to arbitrary positive rational slopes.

papers.title: The Maximum Diagonal Product of a Stochastic Matrix of Bounded Rank
papers.abstract: Let $A=(a_{ij})$ be a nonnegative row-stochastic or column-stochastic $n\times n$ matrix of rank at most $k$, where $1\le k\le n$. Write $n=qk+s$, where $0\le s<k$. The author conjectured in 2018 that, for every permutation $σ$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, $\prod_{i=1}^n a_{i,σ(i)}\le q^{-q(k-s)}(q+1)^{-(q+1)s}$. We prove this bound and classify all equality cases.

papers.title: The quantum double of the restricted quantum group $\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2})$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct the quantum double $D(\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2}))$ of the restricted quantum group $\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2})$. We describe the algebraic structure of $D(\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2}))$ by generators and relations. Moreover, we give the comultiplication $\Delta$, the counit $\varepsilon$ and the antipode $S$, respectively. Finally, we classify all irreducible representations of $D(\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2}))$ when $p=2$.

papers.title: The Schur-Siegel-Smyth trace problem: the lower bound 1.8022246
papers.abstract: We prove lambda_SSS >= 9011123/5000000 = 1.8022246 for the smallest limiting trace-to-degree ratio of totally positive algebraic integers. The previous best bound is 1.8022225 (Tomar). The certificate consists of fourteen integer polynomials with rational multipliers and a continuous piecewise-linear density with 8678 rational hat weights; its dual inequality is verified on (0,infinity) in ball arithmetic. For the same family of polynomials the value of the underlying optimisation problem is 1.8022247 to within 10^-9 (numerical), so the bound is within 1.1*10^-7 of what this family can give.

papers.title: The Wang Transform Inequality
papers.abstract: We prove the Wang transform inequality in every order: if $n$ is a positive integer, $A$ is a nonnegative $n\times n$ matrix whose row and column sums equal one, and $J_n$ has every entry $1/n$, then $\operatorname{per}A\ge \operatorname{per}\!\left(\frac{nJ_n+A}{n+1}\right)$. Equality holds exactly when $A=J_n$. We also obtain an explicit positive quadratic gap for every $n\ge2$.

papers.title: Triangles in sets of positive upper density in the plane
papers.abstract: This note proves that every measurable subset of the plane with positive upper Banach density contains a translate of a rotation of every sufficiently large dilate of any fixed noncollinear triangle.

papers.title: Twisted conjugacy in spherical Artin groups and their crystallographic quotients
papers.abstract: A group has property $R_\infty$ if every automorphism has infinitely many twisted conjugacy classes. Let $A$ be an irreducible spherical Artin group of Coxeter rank at least two, with pure subgroup $P$. We classify property $R_\infty$ for the crystallographic quotient $\Gamma=A/[P,P]$. If $A$ has Coxeter rank at least three, then $\Gamma$ has $R_\infty$. In type $I_2(m)$, this holds exactly when $4\mid m$, or when $m$ is odd and $3\mid m$. Together with the known dihedral Artin-group cases, the positive quotient results imply that every irreducible spherical Artin group of rank at least two has $R_\infty$. The positive proofs combine the rational representation theory of the holonomy action with integral lattice constraints and explicit fixed-vector witnesses. In the negative dihedral cases, we construct automorphisms compatible with the crystallographic extension. For type $I_2(5)$, we exhibit an automorphism with Reidemeister number $18$, showing concretely that the quotient construction does not preserve $R_\infty$. This example, including the identification with the presented Artin quotient and the exact Reidemeister count, is formalised in Lean. An alternative proof for seven Artin groups is formalised under explicitly stated external hypotheses.

papers.title: Two exact frequency extrema for smooth sequences over {1,3}
papers.abstract: Using the frequency coding of Jamet, Marcovici, Poirier, and de la Rue, we determine the largest frequency of $1$ in a smooth sequence over $\{1,3\}$ and the largest such frequency below $1/2$. They are $1/2+1/(3+\sqrt{5})$ and $1/2-1/(13-\sqrt{5})$, respectively. The unique attaining type directives are $1^\infty$ and $0001^\infty$. The proof is an order comparison for two planar homographies. The first value corrects the numerical expression in the stated extremum question.

papers.title: Uniform symmetric spectral finiteness of semialgebraic cones
papers.abstract: Cone-constrained eigenvalues of a matrix are defined through a complementarity problem constrained by a closed convex cone. We show that every closed semialgebraic convex cone is uniformly symmetrically spectrally finite; that is, the cone spectra, the sets of the cone-constrained eigenvalues, of symmetric matrices relative to the cone are uniformly finite with respect to the matrices. The uniform bound is explicit, and as an application, we derive a uniform bound for the cardinality of spectra of symmetric matrices relative to L\"{o}wner cones. In addition, using the uniform finiteness of cone spectra, we also show the uniform finiteness of the number of singular values relative to two closed semialgebraic convex cones. For non-semialgebraic cones, we observe two contrasting phenomena. On the one hand, we show that the exponential cone is uniformly symmetrically spectrally finite. On the other hand, we provide a closed non-semialgebraic convex cone such that the associated cone spectra of symmetric matrices are finite but are not uniformly finite.

papers.title: Unimodal Singularities of Parametrized Space Curves
papers.abstract: The aim of the article is to classify unimodal parametrized space curve singularities defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$. We provide explicit normal forms of parametrizations up to $\mathcal A$-equivalence. The parametrizations are given by convergent power series over a real valued field, which includes parametrizations given by formal power series and by, for example, convergent power series over the complex numbers or the field of Puisieux series. The list of normal forms is surprisingly simple.

papers.title: Virtual Two-Step Nilpotency of the Fundamental Groups of Special Quasi-Projective Varieties
papers.abstract: We prove that the fundamental group of every smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety that is special in the sense of Campana is virtually nilpotent of class at most two. This establishes the two-step nilpotency conjecture of Cao--Deng--Hacon--P\u{a}un, a quasi-projective analogue of Campana's almost abelian conjecture for special compact K\"ahler manifolds. Examples of Cadorel--Deng--Yamanoi show that the step bound is sharp. On a suitable finite etale cover, we construct a canonical second Albanese map to a torus torsor over an abelian variety. The proof reduces to showing that the kernel of the induced map on fundamental groups is finite. Using good minimal models and meridian groups of projective pairs, we show that an infinite kernel would yield a saturated rank-one subsheaf of logarithmic differentials whose Iitaka dimension contradicts specialness.

papers.title: Waldschmidt constants and invariant geometry for exceptional rank-four complex reflection groups
papers.abstract: We compute the Waldschmidt constants of the point configurations dual to the reflection arrangements of the exceptional complex reflection groups $G_{29}$, $G_{31}$ and $G_{32}$. They equal $3$ for the forty points of $G_{29}$, $36/11$ for the sixty-point Klein configuration, and $10/3$ for the forty-point Penrose configuration. Together with the known cases $W(F_4)$ and $W(H_4)$, this completes the computation for all exceptional irreducible complex reflection groups of rank four. An invariant dodecic and its sixfold orbit product give extremal surfaces for the first two configurations, and we identify the six dodecics as pullbacks of the coordinate hyperplane sections of the Segre cubic under the Igusa-Segre duality. The matching lower bounds follow from restriction to quadrics and distinguished planes, including a weighted B\'ezout estimate arising from two related Hesse arrangements. As a consequence, we determine the asymptotic resurgences of the three ideals.

papers.title: Watkins's Conjecture for Elliptic Curves with Rational Two-Torsion
papers.abstract: We prove that the modular degree of every elliptic curve \(E/\mathbb Q\) with \(E(\mathbb Q)[2]\ne 0\) is divisible by \(2^{\operatorname{rank}E(\mathbb Q)}\).

papers.title: Whittaker supermodules for the Takiff superalgebra \mathfrak{osp}(1|2)
papers.abstract: In this article, we classify all simple Whittaker supermodules over the Takiff Lie superalgebra \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)\otimes\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)\), associated with Whittaker characters defined on the even part of its positive nilpotent subalgebra.
